when.title: When can it help?
when.body: Difficulties with emotional expression and regulation, self-esteem, stress, anxiety, grief, life changes or interpersonal conflicts, as well as the need to find a safe space for creation, expression and emotional support.

about.label: About me
about.heading: A short story about me
bioParagraphs: I'm Candela Sahade, a medical doctor with a degree recognised in Spain and a relational art therapist, with experience supporting children and teenagers.

Since I was little, art has been a way of expressing and understanding what I feel. The desire to care led me to medicine and, later, to art therapy, where I found a way to support others through creativity, presence and connection.
Today I bring together art, listening and care to accompany each person on their own journey.

items.question: Do I need to know how to draw?
items.answer: No. Art therapy is not about aesthetic results or artistic skill. The goal isn't to learn to draw or paint, but to use the artistic process as a means.

items.question: From what age can children take part?
Are the sessions online or in person?
items.answer: Both options are available: in person in Barcelona and Sant Cugat, or online (adults only).

items.question: How do I know if art therapy is right for my child?
items.answer: In the first interview we talk about your particular situation and decide together whether this is the right space.

items.question: How long does the therapeutic process last?
items.answer: Every art therapy process is unique, so its length adapts to each person's needs and goals. In general, it can be organised in blocks of 12 sessions.
